title: Can the harness carry one pocket i's changing knowledge without losing its current belief or its history?
hypothesis: A deterministic verifier can reconstruct append-only knowledge chains, select the current head, preserve older revisions as history, and stop on missing parents, mixed lineages, forks, or retractions.

input_contract.lineage_id: one pocket i's history for one topic
input_contract.previous_revision_id: null for the first revision; otherwise the direct parent
input_contract.claim: one human-readable current belief; empty only for retracts
input_contract.evidence_id: pointer to a separately verified evidence capsule
input_contract.learned_at: when this pocket i recorded the revision

rules: Parent links, not timestamps, define revision order.
Only the head of a valid unbranched lineage is current.
Older revisions remain history and are never silently erased.
A retraction has no active claim but keeps the earlier history.
Two heads in one lineage are a fork, not two independent opinions.
Two different lineages on one topic stay separate.
A newer revision is the pocket i's latest belief, not automatic truth.
Every revision must still pass evidence, privacy, applicability, and independence checks elsewhere.
claim_boundary: Synthetic deterministic development test. It tests chain transport and reconstruction, not signatures, hostile peers, source truth, semantic evidence quality, privacy, physical-device networking, or scale.
